claims.text: Introducing SRO precipitates into a homogeneous SiGe alloy increases phonon scattering.
Introducing SRO precipitates reduces the lattice thermal conductivity of SiGe.
Thermal or chemical treatment can induce SRO precipitate formation within a SiGe matrix.
Suitable annealing or processing conditions can promote nucleation and controlled growth of SRO precipitates without excessive grain growth or phase separation.
The intervention produces SRO precipitates distributed within the SiGe lattice.
SRO precipitates act as additional phonon-scattering centers.
Scattering by SRO precipitates reduces the phonon mean free path.
Scattering by SRO precipitates reduces phonon scattering times.
Reduced phonon mean free path and scattering time lead to lower lattice thermal conductivity.
SiGe containing induced SRO precipitates will have measurably lower lattice thermal conductivity than an unprecipitated SiGe control.
The effectiveness of the intervention depends on obtaining a controlled density and size distribution of SRO precipitates.
Outside the suitable processing range, the conductivity-reduction effect may diminish or be offset by competing phenomena.
The magnitude of conductivity reduction depends on the precipitate distribution, size, and volume fraction.
TEM and XRD can be used to confirm the presence or absence of the proposed SRO precipitates.
Laser flash analysis or a similar method can provide the lattice thermal-conductivity measurement required by the test.
